newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish PBK bank sale decision seen delayed a week.
newsitem.headline: Polish PBK bank sale decision seen delayed a week.

text.p: The Polish government is likely to choose an investor for 10 to 65 percent of Powszechny Bank Kredytowy SA (PBK) at its session next week, the government spokeswoman Aleksandra Jakubowska said on Monday.

She said the cabinet was unlikely to discuss the PBK sell-off on Tuesday, as earlier planned, because Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz had not yet got the information he wanted from the treasury on details of the sale.

"The government will most likely discuss it (the PBK sell-off) at its session next week. The prime minister has not yet received the information he had requested. Maybe he will get it later today," Jakubowska told Reuters.

A source close the government said the prime minister wanted to know why the treasury ministry wanted to sell a stake in PBK to a Polish consortium rather than to South Korea's Samsung Group, even though it had offered a better price for the bank.
"The prime minister has asked why an offer that envisages a worse price has been chosen," the source, who asked not to be named, told Reuters.
The Polish consortium, bidding for at least 51 percent of PBK, groups Bank Przemyslowo-Handlowy BPH, Kredyt Bank and insurer Warta.
Samsung Life Insurance -- a subsidiary of South Korea's Samsung which is bidding for a stake in PBK -- said it hoped the Polish government would make a rational decision.

"We presented the best terms we can and are now just waiting for the results to come. We hope a rational judgement will be made." Cho Jang-won, manager of the group's public information department, told Reuters in Seoul.
Earlier this month the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) said it was willing to buy up to 15 percent of the bank.
The government plans to float another 15 percent of PBK on the Warsaw bourse and the bank's issue prospectus was submitted to the Securities Commission last week.

HSBC Investment Services, which is advising the government on the privatisation, said the stake was likely to hit the bourse in October. It estimated the bank's total value at between 1.2 billion zlotys and 1.6 billion zlotys ($366.7-$489 million).
